Hi Alicia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — really enjoyed digging into Brightline's ingestion profile and latency targets. I promised to follow up with a concrete mutual action plan (MAP) + an initial ramp schedule so your procurement team can align internal approvals.

Attached: Brightline_MAP_v3.pdf (MAP draft)

High level proposal (summary):
- Evaluation window: 4 weeks (pilot, functional tests, SLO smoke tests)
- Pilot target: 10M tokens in month 1 to validate latency and KV caching
- Onramp cadence: month 2 -> 25M TPM, month 3 -> 50M TPM, month 4 onwards -> 100M TPM committed (monthly).
- Pricing triggers: baseline $0.0009/token, at 75% of committed TPM for two consecutive months reduce to $0.0008/token; >=100% commit sustained for 3 months unlocks an additional 5% uplift discount.
- Review gates: weekly syncs during pilot; milestone review at the end of months 1, 3, and 6.

Request: can procurement confirm target close date for the SOW and whether a single-signature DocuSign flow is acceptable? I included a short SOW draft and a timeline in the MAP. If we get verbal authorization by the end of next week we can start provisioning dedicated capacity the following Monday.

Next steps: I can walk procurement through the MAP and pricing triggers in a 30-min call — are you available next Tue/Wed?

Thanks,
Ben

2) Can you confirm whether the pricing trigger at 75% is retroactive for that month or applies going forward?

Alicia — thanks, great questions. Short answers below and I pasted the MAP appendix with explicit waterfall language.

1) Missed milestone remediation: we propose a performance credit model — if a monthly TPM is below target by >=15% for two consecutive months we apply a one-time credit equal to 10% of that month's invoice. There is a catch-up window (60 days) where we prioritize capacity to help you hit the next milestone. If after the catch-up window you remain below target, the committed tier will be recalibrated down (with 30-day notice).

2) Pricing trigger timing: discounts apply prospectively from the month following the attainment threshold. Exception: if you retroactively exceed a commit in a month and sustain for 2 months, we can apply a one-time invoice adjustment for the first month (to reflect the higher tier) — subject to standard audit checks.

3) Logs & audit: during pilot we retain token-level traces for 30 days; committed customers default to 365-day retention with options for exports to your S3 and HSM-integrated KMS for keying. I'll have our security rep send a checklist doc before the sync.

Attached: SOW_Brightline_Draft.docx (SOW with proposed payment schedule and termination language).

Alicia, I've updated the MAP appendix with explicit month-by-month TPMs and the credit language. Proposed month schedule (example):
- Month 0 (pilot): 10M TPM
- Month 1 (onramp): 25M TPM
- Month 2: 50M TPM
- Month 3+: 100M TPM committed (minimum 3-month sustain to lock final discount tiers)

If that looks OK I'm happy to get procurement's signature next week and route the SOW via DocuSign single-signer flow.

Best,
Ben

Ben / Rishi — quick internal note before we finalize:

- I'm OK with the proposed credit model (10% one-time credit after two months below threshold) but recommend we cap exposure to 3 months of credits for the pilot/onramp period. Beyond that we should trigger a commercial review.
- Offer a temporary 5% ramp discount during months 2–4 if they sign SOW within 7 days of DocuSign receipt — this is targeted to accelerate conversion.
- Add an escape clause: if Brightline fails to reach 50% of the month-3 target for three consecutive months post-commit, Redwood reserves the right to reduce dedicated capacity allocation after a 30-day remediation window. This avoids indefinite over-provisioning.

Also suggest we include a one-time performance-driven credit (catch-up credit) if our infra fails to meet the agreed SLOs for two consecutive weeks during pilot — helps neutralize customer concerns and keeps the conversation focused on adoption.

If you want to offer a slightly larger discount, let's reserve an additional 2.5% authority for the AE to use at close. Otherwise we keep the 5% time-limited ramp discount.

Thanks,
Laura
